screenings.clinical_recommendation: Baseline fundus examination normal. Annual follow-up advised.

quality.guidance: Image quality is acceptable for clinical AI screening.

all_predictions.description: Evidence of retinal microvascular damage: dot and blot hemorrhages, microaneurysms, hard exudates, or localized cotton-wool ischemic patches secondary to diabetic microangiopathy.
Confluent drusen deposits (yellow extracellular sub-RPE debris) in the central macula, retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) hyperpigmentation or geographic atrophy risking central visual acuity.
Clear optic disc margins, normal cup-to-disc ratio (<0.4), healthy macula with crisp foveal reflex, and intact retinal vasculature without microaneurysms or hard exudates.
Elevated optic cup-to-disc ratio (>0.6) with vertical elongation, neuroretinal rim thinning, and potential retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) bundle defects indicating progressive optic neuropathy.
Opacification of the crystalline crystalline lens, light scattering, nuclear sclerosis, or cortical hazing diminishing retinal visualization and degrading optical clarity.

screenings.clinical_recommendation: Borderline indicators detected for Diabetic Retinopathy. Non-urgent specialist consultation recommended for diagnostic confirmation and baseline mapping.
screenings.clinical_notes: Moderate NPDR confirmed with focal lipid exudates in macular vicinity. Glycemic control and 6-month follow-up advised.
